sections.h2: What is the fastest way to sell in San Marcos?
sections.html:
San Marcos sellers have three routes: hire an agent, go it alone, or accept cash. The best fit depends mostly on the condition of the house and how soon you need to close. A college town on the Interstate 35 corridor between Austin and San Antonio has steady buyer traffic, but a home that needs work or carries an unpaid tax bill can still sit.

San Marcos is the Hays County seat, about 25 miles south of Austin on I-35, according to the Texas State Historical Association. The city also reaches into Guadalupe County, which matters because two different appraisal districts may handle parcels here. Check which district covers your lot before you read a tax statement.

A cash sale trims the steps that slow a listing: showings, buyer financing, lender appraisals and repair negotiations. The trade is a price below what a fully repaired, well staged listing might bring. Ask for a written offer, read what it says about repairs and closing costs, and compare it with what an agent would net after commission.

sections.h2: What does the San Marcos housing market look like?
sections.html:
San Marcos is a renter-heavy city. Census QuickFacts shows only 30.8 percent of homes lived in by their owners for 2020 to 2024, and a median home value of $310,400.

Those figures sit beside a few others that shape how a seller should think about buyers:

  • Estimated population on July 1, 2025: 77,830, up 14.9 percent from the April 2020 estimates base.
  • Households in 2020 to 2024: 28,013, with 2.28 persons per household.
  • Median gross rent: $1,322 a month.
  • Median selected monthly owner costs with a mortgage: $1,899; without a mortgage: $706.
  • Land area: 35.59 square miles, or 1,898 people per square mile in 2020.

With so many renters, investors who buy houses to rent out are a large part of the demand for older or rough homes. That helps a seller whose house needs a new roof or foundation work, since those buyers expect to price the repairs in.

sections.h2: What do the Census numbers say about San Marcos buyers?
sections.html:
Census QuickFacts describes a young, student-influenced city. Persons under 18 are 13.3 percent of the population, and 10.8 percent are 65 or older. Veterans number 2,911 for 2020 to 2024.

Money figures show why price matters. Median household income is $51,281, per capita income is $27,545 in 2024 dollars, and 26.9 percent of people are in poverty. Mean travel time to work is 24.0 minutes, and 38.3 percent of adults 25 and older hold a bachelor's degree or higher.

Retail activity is large for the city's size. QuickFacts lists total retail sales of $3,769,202 thousand for 2022, which comes to $53,551 per capita. Broadband subscriptions reach 85.3 percent of households.

For a seller, those numbers suggest a pool of renters and first time buyers watching monthly cost closely. Homes that rent easily, with working systems and few surprises, are easier to sell to them.

sections.h2: How did San Marcos grow, and why does it matter to a seller?
sections.html:
The town grew around the San Marcos Springs and the river, and the Texas Handbook traces its commercial life to the arrival of the International-Great Northern Railroad on August 31, 1880. Education became a local industry after the state chartered a normal school in 1899, and that school opened in 1903 as Southwest Texas State Normal School, the school that later grew into Southwest Texas State University.

The Handbook says education became the single largest employer in the city during the 1960s, and that Hays County joined the Austin metropolitan area in 1973. It also notes that by the mid 1980s at least 20 percent of the county labor force worked in Travis County.

For a seller, this means demand follows the academic calendar and Austin commuting patterns. Houses near campus and houses near the highway attract different buyers, so ask for offers that explain how the price was set.

sections.h2: Which San Marcos schools and rules affect your sale?
sections.html:
San Marcos ISD is one of the school districts the Guadalupe Appraisal District lists among the units it appraises for. Buyers with children usually ask which district a house sits in, so have that answer ready.

The city also regulates rentals. San Marcos Code Compliance states that owners of short term and long term rentals inside the city must register the property under city ordinances, and its officers patrol more than 30 square miles. When you sell a rental, the registration status is worth confirming with the city before you set a closing date, because a buyer or title company may ask for it. Report or ask about code issues through the Code Compliance line at 512-393-8479.

sections.h2: How do property taxes and exemptions work when you sell in San Marcos?
sections.html:
Hays County parcels are appraised by the Hays Central Appraisal District, which does not send bills or take payments. The Hays County Tax Office handles bills and payments, and the tax office says it has no say over appraised values or exemptions.

No state property tax exists in Texas, so every figure comes from local units. Each year's tax lien starts January 1, so the proration line on your closing statement deserves a careful read.

Texas property tax dates that apply to a San Marcos house (Texas Comptroller)
DateWhat happens
January 1Value is set and the tax lien attaches
April 1 or soon afterAppraisal notices go out for homesteads
May 15Typical protest filing deadline with the appraisal review board
October 1Bills are mailed
January 31Payment deadline before penalties; delinquent from February 1

The Comptroller prints a $140,000 school homestead exemption, with another $60,000 for senior or disabled owners. Hays CAD also audits every granted homestead once every five years, so a seller who moved out should not leave the exemption running.

sections.h2: How is a San Marcos deed recorded?
sections.html:
Deeds are filed by the clerk of whichever county holds the parcel, and the signature needs a notary or similar officer. The Texas courts manual prints a $5.00 charge for page one and $4.00 for each page after it.

Inherited houses add a step. Depending on the estate, the title company will ask for an executor's deed, a court order paired with the will, or an affidavit of death with the certificate when a transfer on death deed exists. Settle which one applies before you accept an offer, since the wrong document can add weeks.

sections.h2: What if the house has a lender, a lease or repair needs?
sections.html:
A lender default, a tenant and a failing roof each run on their own clock, and a cash purchaser can often work inside it. Texas foreclosure is mostly nonjudicial, with a notice of sale and a public auction, so a private sale before the auction date may protect your equity.

For a rental, the landlord needs written notice and a justice court order before a tenant can be removed. Some buyers will simply take the lease. For repairs, an as is purchase moves the work and the contractor bids to the buyer.

faqs.q: Do San Marcos repairs have to be finished before a sale?
faqs.a: No. An investor can take the house in its current shape, and you decide whether the net offer beats a repaired listing. Compare a written offer against an agent's estimate of net proceeds after commission and repairs.

faqs.q: Who sends the property tax bill for a San Marcos home?
faqs.a: The tax office of the county where the parcel sits sends it. In Hays County that is the Hays County Tax Office, and the Hays Central Appraisal District only sets values and exemptions. Bills go out around October 1 and are delinquent after January 31.

faqs.q: Do I need to register a San Marcos rental before selling it?
faqs.a: San Marcos Code Compliance says owners of short term and long term rentals must register under city ordinances. Confirm your registration status with the city, since a buyer or title company may ask about it.

faqs.q: How long does a cash sale take in San Marcos?
faqs.a: The timeline depends on title work and the buyer, so ask for a closing date in writing. Probate, liens or unpaid taxes can add time, and a clear title usually moves the fastest.

faqs.q: Does the homestead exemption end when I sell?
faqs.a: Someone who closes after January 1 may claim the exemption for the remaining months of that year when the earlier owner had none, per the Comptroller. Tell the Hays Central Appraisal District that you moved out so its records stay accurate.
